traceability.evidence:
Implementation and tests exist and are wired to this story:
1) Direct story linkage in code and tests - src/maintenance/index.ts - JSDoc: - `@story docs/stories/009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS.story.md` - `@req REQ-MAINT-DETECT`, `REQ-MAINT-UPDATE`, `REQ-MAINT-BATCH`, `REQ-MAINT-VERIFY`, `REQ-MAINT-REPORT`, `REQ-MAINT-SAFE` - Re-exports: detectStaleAnnotations, updateAnnotationReferences, batchUpdateAnnotations, verifyAnnotations, generateMaintenanceReport - src/index.ts - Imports all maintenance functions from "./maintenance" and exposes them via a `maintenance` export - JSDoc: - `@story docs/stories/009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS.story.md` - `@req REQ-MAINTENANCE-API-EXPORT - Expose maintenance utilities alongside core plugin exports` - tests/maintenance/*.test.ts all include: - `* @story docs/stories/009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS.story.md` - `@req` tags mapping to REQ-MAINT-* requirement IDs
2) REQ-MAINT-DETECT: Detect stale annotation references - Implementation: src/maintenance/detect.ts - `detectStaleAnnotations(codebasePath: string): string[]` scans all files under a workspace root, finds `@story` annotations, and adds story paths to a `stale` set when no in-project candidate file exists. - Uses `getAllFiles(workspaceRoot)` to traverse the workspace. - Guards for invalid/nonexistent workspace root: - `if (!fs.existsSync(workspaceRoot) || !fs.statSync(workspaceRoot).isDirectory()) { return []; }` - Per-file processing: - `processFileForStaleAnnotations` reads file content (with try/catch to ignore read errors) and iterates regex `@story\s+([^\s]+)` matches. - `handleStoryMatch` performs security checks via `isUnsafeStoryPath` (skips traversal/absolute/invalid-extension paths), enforces project boundary via `enforceProjectBoundary`, and only checks `fs.existsSync` for in-project candidates. - Behavior & edge case tests: - tests/maintenance/detect.test.ts - `[REQ-MAINT-DETECT] should return empty array when no stale annotations` creating an empty tmp dir; expects `[]`. - `[REQ-MAINT-DETECT] should detect stale annotation references` writing `@story stale.story.md` into a file; expects result length 1 and contains "stale.story.md". - tests/maintenance/detect-isolated.test.ts - `[REQ-MAINT-DETECT] returns empty array when directory does not exist` calling `detectStaleAnnotations("non-existent-dir")` and expecting `[]`. - `[REQ-MAINT-DETECT] detects stale annotations in nested directories` creates nested dirs and two files with different stale stories; expects both story names and length 2. - Permission edge case: creates subdir, writes file, chmod to 0o000, then `expect(() => detectStaleAnnotations(tmpDir2)).toThrow()`; plus cleanup. - Security validation test ensuring no filesystem existence checks run for malicious or invalid story paths: - Writes a file containing `@story ../outside-project.story.md`, `@story /etc/passwd.story.md`, `@story invalid.txt`, `@story legitimate.story.md` etc. - Spies on `fs.existsSync` and asserts none of the malicious or invalid paths (raw or resolved) were checked, while ensuring only legitimate in-workspace `.story.md` paths are checked.
3) REQ-MAINT-UPDATE: Update annotation references when story files move/rename - Implementation: src/maintenance/update.ts - `updateAnnotationReferences(codebasePath: string, oldPath: string, newPath: string): number` - Early exit if `codebasePath` does not exist or is not a directory: returns 0. - Escapes `oldPath` for regex and builds `new RegExp((@story\s*)${escapedOldPath}, "g")`. - Uses `getAllFiles(codebasePath)` to enumerate files and for each file calls `processFileForAnnotationUpdates`. - Returns the count of replacements performed (via `replacementCountRef.count`). - `processFileForAnnotationUpdates`: - Skips non-files using `fs.statSync(fullPath).isFile()`. - Reads file, runs `.replace(regex, (match, p1) => { replacementCountRef.count++; return `${p1}${newPath}`; })`. - Only writes back to disk if content changed (`if (newContent !== content) writeFileSync`). - Tests: - tests/maintenance/update-isolated.test.ts - `[REQ-MAINT-UPDATE] updates @story annotations in files`: - Writes a ts file with `@story old.path.md`, runs `updateAnnotationReferences(tmpDir, "old.path.md", "new.path.md")`, expects count 1 and verifies file now contains `@story new.path.md`. - `[REQ-MAINT-UPDATE] should return 0 when directory does not exist`: - Calls `updateAnnotationReferences("non-existent-dir", "old.md", "new.md")` and expects 0. - tests/maintenance/update.test.ts - `[REQ-MAINT-UPDATE] should return 0 when no updates made` using an empty dir; expects count 0.
4) REQ-MAINT-BATCH & REQ-MAINT-VERIFY: Batch updates and verification - Implementation: src/maintenance/batch.ts - `batchUpdateAnnotations(codebasePath: string, mappings: { oldPath: string; newPath: string }[]): number` - Loops over mappings and accumulates `updateAnnotationReferences(codebasePath, oldPath, newPath)` into `totalUpdated`. - `verifyAnnotations(codebasePath: string): boolean` - Calls `detectStaleAnnotations(codebasePath)` and returns true if length === 0. - Tests: - tests/maintenance/batch.test.ts - `[REQ-MAINT-BATCH] should return 0 when no mappings applied` calling `batchUpdateAnnotations(tmpDir, [])` and expecting 0. - `[REQ-MAINT-VERIFY] should return true when annotations are valid`: - Prepares tmp dir with a ts file referencing `my-story.story.md` and a matching story file. - Asserts `verifyAnnotations(tmpDir)` returns true.
5) REQ-MAINT-REPORT & REQ-MAINT-SAFE: Reporting and safety - Implementation: src/maintenance/report.ts - `generateMaintenanceReport(codebasePath: string): string` - Calls `detectStaleAnnotations(codebasePath)`. - If no stale annotations: returns empty string (`""`). - Otherwise: returns `staleAnnotations.join("\n")` — newline-separated list. - Tests: - tests/maintenance/report.test.ts - `[REQ-MAINT-REPORT] should return empty string when no operations` calling `generateMaintenanceReport(tmpDir)` for fresh dir; expects `""`. - `[REQ-MAINT-REPORT] should report stale story annotation`: - Writes a stub file containing `@story non-existent.story.md`, then expects report to contain that story.
6) CLI and user experience (Core Functionality, UX, Error Handling, Batch/Verify/Report/Update integration) - Implementation: src/maintenance/cli.ts - Exposed via `bin` in package.json: `"traceability-maint": "lib/src/maintenance/cli.js"`. - Entry: `runMaintenanceCli(rawArgv: string[]): number` with a shebang for CLI use. - Commands handled: - `detect` → `handleDetect` - `verify` → `handleVerify` - `report` → `handleReport` - `update` → `handleUpdate` - `-h` / `--help` or missing command → `printHelp()` and exit 0 - Unknown command → error message + help + exit usage code 2 - Error handling: - Wraps command dispatch in try/catch; on error prints concise diagnostic and returns EXIT_USAGE (2). - Flag parsing (`parseFlags`, `applyFlag`, `createDefaultFlags`): - Supports `--root`, `--json`, `--format text|json`, `--from`, `--to`, `--dry-run`. - `handleDetect`: - Calls `detectStaleAnnotations(root)`. - If `--json`, prints `JSON.stringify({ root, stale })`. - Else prints a friendly “No stale @story annotations found.” message or lists stale stories and a summary with count and hint to run `report`. - Exit code: 0 when no stale annotations, 1 when stale entries exist. - `handleVerify`: - Calls `verifyAnnotations(root)`. - On valid: prints success message and exit 0. - On invalid: prints advisory message and exit 1. - `handleReport`: - Uses `generateMaintenanceReport(root)`. - `--format json` prints JSON: `{ root, report }`. - Text mode prints either "No stale @story annotations found. Nothing to report." or a Markdown-like heading plus list. - Always exit 0. - `handleUpdate`: - Validates `--from` and `--to` are provided; otherwise prints error and help, exits with usage code 2. - For `--dry-run`: - Calls `generateMaintenanceReport(root)` to estimate potential stale annotations, and prints a summary (either JSON or text) without modifying files. - Exit 0. - Without `--dry-run`: - Calls `updateAnnotationReferences(root, from, to)`, then prints JSON or human-readable text summarizing how many annotations were updated. - Exit 0. - Tests: tests/maintenance/cli.test.ts - `[REQ-MAINT-DETECT] detect exits with code 0 and message when no stale annotations`. - Asserts exit code 0 and `console.log` called with "No stale @story annotations found.". - `[REQ-MAINT-VERIFY] verify exits with code 0 when annotations valid`. - Sets up valid story+code; expects exit 0 and one log call. - `[REQ-MAINT-REPORT] report prints human-readable summary and exits 0`. - Creates stale reference and expects log output containing "Traceability Maintenance Report" and the missing story name; exit 0. - `[REQ-MAINT-UPDATE] update performs replacements and exits 0`. - Ensures CLI `update` modifies file content from `old.path.md` to `new.path.md` and exit 0. - `[REQ-MAINT-SAFE] update requires --from and --to and exits 2 when missing`. - Checks that missing args yield exit code 2 and both `console.error` and `console.log` (help) are called. - `[REQ-MAINT-SAFE] dry-run does not modify files and exits 0`. - Confirms `--dry-run` mode leaves file unchanged and exits 0. - `[REQ-MAINT-DETECT] detect supports --json output`. - With a stale story present and `--json`, ensures exit code 1, exactly one log call, payload with `stale` array containing the stale story.
7) Core Functionality acceptance criterion - Detection: `detectStaleAnnotations` plus `traceability-maint detect` and tests (detect.test.ts, detect-isolated.test.ts, cli.test.ts) show tools can locate stale references based on missing story files, including nested dirs. - Update: `updateAnnotationReferences` plus `traceability-maint update` and tests (update-isolated.test.ts, update.test.ts, cli.test.ts) confirm annotations are updated when story paths change. - Batch & verify: `batchUpdateAnnotations` and `verifyAnnotations` in src/maintenance/batch.ts plus tests in batch.test.ts satisfy bulk operations and post-update verification.
8) Quality Standards acceptance criterion - Update logic only rewrites `@story` paths, preserving all other code, and only writes files when content changes (minimizing formatting/whitespace churn). - Tests verify that produced files remain syntactically valid (e.g., update-isolated.test.ts re-reads the TypeScript file without parse issues) and that dry-run mode leaves files unchanged.
9) Integration with project structure and ESLint configuration - src/index.ts exports `maintenance` object alongside `rules` and `configs`, making maintenance functions available from the main plugin API. - package.json `bin` entry wires the CLI: `"traceability-maint": "lib/src/maintenance/cli.js"`. - README.md documents `traceability-maint` usage under "Maintenance CLI" with command examples (`detect`, `verify`, `report`, `update`) and refers to user-docs/api-reference.md#maintenance-api-and-cli for full details, confirming that tools are integrated into the documented workflow.
10) User Experience acceptance criterion - CLI provides clear, human-readable messages: - Success/empty states ("No stale @story annotations found.", "No stale @story annotations found. Nothing to report.") - Markdown-style report headings ("# Traceability Maintenance Report for ...") - Summaries for update operations (`Updated X @story annotation(s) from ...`). - Clear error messages for misuse (missing `--from`/`--to`, unknown commands) and a rich help message printed by `printHelp()`. - JSON output modes (`--json`, `--format json`) support tool integration while still providing readable text defaults. - Tests in tests/maintenance/cli.test.ts assert both messaging and exit codes for all subcommands.
11) Error Handling acceptance criterion - Non-existent directories: detect and update return non-throwing safe results ([], 0) with explicit tests. - Permission issues: detect-isolated.test.ts exercises a permission-denied scenario and checks for thrown errors; CLI runMaintenanceCli wraps execution in try/catch and converts such errors into concise diagnostics and a non-zero exit code. - Invalid flags: `handleUpdate` validates required flags and returns EXIT_USAGE with error messages and help; CLI also handles unknown commands gracefully. - Security/edge-case handling: detect-isolated.test.ts asserts that malicious or invalid @story paths do not trigger filesystem checks, ensuring safety for paths that escape workspace boundaries.
12) Documentation acceptance criterion - README.md (lines 100–134) has a dedicated "Maintenance CLI" section: - Describes `traceability-maint` purpose: "maintain and audit `@story` annotations". - Lists commands: detect, verify, report, update. - Provides concrete usage examples and explains `--root`, `--format`, etc. - Links to `user-docs/api-reference.md#maintenance-api-and-cli` for full details and JSON payloads. - This satisfies the requirement for usage examples and best practices at the user-doc level.
13) Tests and execution status - Multiple test files are dedicated to this story: tests/maintenance/detect.test.ts, detect-isolated.test.ts, update.test.ts, update-isolated.test.ts, batch.test.ts, report.test.ts, cli.test.ts, index.test.ts, all tagged with `@story docs/stories/009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS.story.md` and requirement IDs. - `npm test -- --verbose` runs `jest --ci --bail --verbose` and returns without error output, indicating the test suite (including all maintenance tests) passes under CI-style conditions.
